pages.name: The shadow
pages.text: Here `a` is `3i + 4j` and `b` is `4i`. A light shines square onto `b`'s line, so `a` casts a [[shadow]] along it. The shadow is `|a|` cos θ, the side next to θ, just as when you resolve. Here it is 3, and `b` is 4 long. Multiply them and you get the [[dot product]], `a·b` = `|a||b|` cos θ = 3 × 4 = 12.

pages.name: A longer b
pages.task: Now `b` is `6i`, and `a` is still `3i + 4j`. What is `a·b`?
pages.why: The shadow of `a` on `b`'s line is still 3 long, and `b` is 6 long. So `a·b` = 3 × 6 = 18. It is a plain number, because a shadow is a length.

pages.name: Swing it round
pages.text: As `a` swings round, its shadow shrinks to a dot at 90°. So two arrows square to each other give `a·b` = 0. Past 90° the shadow falls behind the start and counts as minus.

pages.name: At 120°
pages.task: `a` is 5 long and `b` is 4 long, with 120° between them. What is `a·b`?
pages.why: cos 120° is −0.5. So the shadow is 5 × (−0.5) = −2.5, behind the start. Then `a·b` = −2.5 × 4 = −10. The arrows lean apart, so the answer is negative.

pages.name: Part by part
pages.text: `i` is 1 long and lies along its own line, so `i·i` = 1. `j` is square to `i` and casts no shadow on it, so `i·j` = 0. Now multiply every part of `3i + 4j` by every part of `4i + 3j`. That gives `3i·4i`, `3i·3j`, `4j·4i` and `4j·3j`. The two crossed pairs give 0. The matching pairs give 12 and 12, so the dot product is 24.

pages.name: Pulling back
pages.task: A crate slides 3 m along the deck, in the `i` direction. A rope pulls on it with `−40i + 30j` N. How much work does the rope do?
pages.why: The move is `3i` m. Pair the parts. −40 × 3 + 30 × 0 = −120 J. The rope pulls against the move, so its work is negative.
